name: bottom-sheet
title: Bottom Sheet
description: A panel that rises from the bottom edge, rests at one of several heights (snap points), and can be dragged between them or down to dismiss, with a keyboard handle that does the same.

meta.when: Phones first: details, filters, a picker or a secondary task that should stay within reach of the thumb and may be peeked at before it is opened fully. With `modal={false}` it stays open while the page behind is used (a player, a route summary). For a panel from a side edge, or one with no snap points on a desktop, use sheet; for a short decision use dialog; beside the content on wide screens use dock. Always give it a BottomSheetTitle (add className="sr-only" to hide it). Opened by state with no BottomSheetTrigger, focus does not return on close: refocus the opener in `onCloseAutoFocus` on BottomSheetContent.
meta.example:
<BottomSheet snapPoints={[0.4, 0.9]}>
  <BottomSheetTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Details</Button></BottomSheetTrigger>
  <BottomSheetContent>
    <BottomSheetHandle />
    <BottomSheetHeader>
      <BottomSheetTitle>Saturday</BottomSheetTitle>
      <BottomSheetDescription>Three things planned.</BottomSheetDescription>
    </BottomSheetHeader>
    <BottomSheetBody>…</BottomSheetBody>
    <BottomSheetFooter>
      <BottomSheetClose asChild><Button>Done</Button></BottomSheetClose>
    </BottomSheetFooter>
  </BottomSheetContent>
</BottomSheet>

// Controlled, in pixels and rems, staying open while the page is used
<BottomSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={["6rem", "320px", 1]} snap={snap} onSnapChange={setSnap} modal={false} dismissible={false}>
  …
</BottomSheet>
